short: Moving the king to safety and bringing a rook into the game, in one move.
body: Castling does two jobs at once, which is why it is the best move-for-move value in the opening. The king leaves the centre file, which is where lines open first, and a rook arrives at d1 or f1 where it actually does something.

Almost every trap in this library only works against a king still on e1 or e8. Castling by about move eight is not a superstition — it is the move that switches the tactics off. If you are ever unsure what to play in the opening and your king is still at home, castling is rarely wrong.
The right to castle is worth something even before you use it. Losing it — by moving the king or a rook — is a real concession, and this app's king-safety measure drops when it happens.

diagram.caption: Both kings tucked away, both rooks brought toward the centre.
